findings.summary: The page contradicts itself about when springdoc scans controllers.
findings.evidence: The diagram says "Startup scan", but the note below it says "springdoc scans controllers on first docs request".
findings.fix: Use one account of the timing on both lines. Say springdoc builds the spec from the controllers when the app runs, and generates it lazily on the first /v3/api-docs request. Rename the diagram step to match.

findings.summary: The pipeline diagram and its caption mix an ambiguous "on first docs request" note, and the page says nothing about which URL triggers the scan versus the UI.
findings.evidence: springdoc scans controllers on first docs request / Swagger UI only renders the spec / A basic spec needs no code changes
findings.fix: Label the diagram arrows (scan, serve spec, render) and keep the three notes as separate one-line bullets under the diagram.

findings.summary: The Gotchas section bundles several ideas into arrows and a closing rule, so the cause and effect for each wrong-library case are unclear.
findings.evidence: Wrong starter on Boot 3 → blank UI or startup errors / springfox on the classpath → same breakage
findings.fix: Use a small table with columns Mistake | Symptom | Fix.

findings.summary: The example puts @Tag on a method, but the table says it belongs on the controller, so the example does not show correct placement.
findings.evidence: The table says "@Tag(name) | controller", but the example lists "@Tag(name = \"Users\")" directly above "@Operation(summary = \"Get user\")" and "@GetMapping(\"/users/{id}\")".
findings.fix: Show a class declaration such as `@Tag(name = "Users") @RestController class UserController {` and keep @Operation and @ApiResponse on the method. Add a comment that @Tag sits on the class.

findings.summary: Global info and Bearer JWT setup are described as code fragments in prose bullets, and a bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Global info: an @Bean OpenAPI with new OpenAPI().info(new Info().title(...).version(...))
findings.fix: State the idea in one line ("declare one OpenAPI bean for title, version and security"), then show a short code block with both info and the security scheme.

findings.summary: The @Schema bullet packs four attributes and two target types into one line, and the example code block mixes class-level and field-level snippets, with a caption to explain it.
findings.evidence: @Schema(description, example, requiredMode, accessMode) on DTO classes and fields / the last line sits on the DTO field
findings.fix: Split the example into a controller block and a separate DTO block, and move the attributes to a small table.

findings.summary: A gotcha bullet holds two ideas about error types and their link to the earlier bullet is unclear.
findings.evidence: Error types from @RestControllerAdvice get documented as responses
findings.fix: State it as one idea: "@RestControllerAdvice handlers appear automatically as error responses", and drop the repeat in the Remember box if it is unclear.

findings.summary: The Key Properties YAML is shown before the idea behind it, and its one-line explanation is a dense list of four settings.
findings.evidence: spec path, UI path, sort operations by method, tags A-Z
findings.fix: Add a one-line lead-in before the block and turn the four explanations into a small property | effect table.

findings.summary: The security bullets mix two options in one bullet, and the prod switch note is a caption rather than a statement of the idea.
findings.evidence: Either permitAll them, or protect them deliberately
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: dev/internal uses permitAll; prod keeps them protected or disabled. State the idea before the YAML.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold more than one idea, and the XML appender is shown as one compressed block with several tags on one line.
findings.evidence: Rolling policy rotates by date and size; totalSizeCap stops a full disk / </rollingPolicy><encoder><pattern>%d %p %c %m%n</pattern></encoder>
findings.fix: Split the rolling bullet into rotation and cap; format the XML with one tag per line.

findings.summary: The Remember box uses garbled wording that could be misread.
findings.evidence: Appenders: they add up up the tree unless additivity is false.
findings.fix: Write: "Appenders accumulate up the logger tree unless additivity is false."

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "automatically", "reference").
findings.evidence: MDC is a per-thread map: MDC.put("traceId", id) then reference it in the pattern with %X{traceId}; JSON encoders add all MDC entries as fields automatically
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "onceperrequestfilter", "generates").
findings.evidence: Pattern: a OncePerRequestFilter reads X-Request-Id (or generates a UUID), puts it into MDC, sets the response header, and calls MDC.remove or MDC.clear in a finally block
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The JSON section places a Boot 3.4+ detail before the version table and calls it "Pre-3.4" in a bullet that mixes two ideas.
findings.fix: Put the version table first, then add a separate bullet for adding custom fields with kv().

findings.summary: The MDC filter code is long and is shown before the idea is stated in one line, and the bullet on Micrometer sits under a stray heading.
findings.evidence: inside a OncePerRequestFilter / Micrometer Tracing / Boot auto-populates traceId and spanId in MDC.
findings.fix: Add a one-line lead-in ("Filter sets traceId, always clears it") before the code, and fold the Micrometer note into the Gotchas list.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet is labelled with a Log Levels bullet list mixing config, runtime and appender facts, and the JSON/MDC code repeats page 5 without new information.
findings.evidence: logback-spring.xml handles profiles and appenders / Rolling policy needs totalSizeCap
findings.fix: Turn section 3 into a table (Need | Setting) and keep only the code that is not already a one-line fact.
